script:
dest=old; declare -n ref=dest
dest=a ref+=b /bin/sh -c 'printf "dest=<%s> mid=<%s> ref=<%s> a=<%s> b=<%s>\n" "$dest" "$mid" "$ref" "$a" "$b"'

name: an integer name through a name that holds it, appended to
script:
declare -i x=5; declare -n ref=x
ref+=3+4 /bin/sh -c 'echo "x=<$x>"'; echo "after=<$x>"

name: an integer name through a name that holds it
script:
declare -i x=5; declare -n ref=x
ref=3+4 /bin/sh -c 'echo "x=<$x>"'

name: an integer name appended to twice
script:
declare -i x=5; declare -n ref=x
ref+=3+4 x+=1 /bin/sh -c 'echo "x=<$x>"'

name: an integer name assigned, then appended to
script:
declare -i x=5
x=1 x+=2+3 /bin/sh -c 'echo "x=<$x>"'

name: an integer name appended to with a side effect
script:
declare -i x=5; n=2
x+=n++ /bin/sh -c 'echo "x=<$x>"'; echo "n=$n"

name: an integer name appended to with a division by zero
script:
declare -i x=5
x+=1/0 /bin/echo RAN >out; echo "same-line S=$?"
echo next-line S=$?
bash:
1/0: division by 0 (error token is "0")
next-line S=1

name: an integer name appended to with a syntax error
script:
declare -i x=5
x+='3+' /bin/echo RAN; echo "same S=$?"
echo next S=$?
bash:
3+: arithmetic syntax error: operand expected (error token is "+")
next S=1
bash_5_2:
3+: syntax error: operand expected (error token is "+")
next S=1

name: an integer name appended to with nothing
script:
declare -i x=5
x+= /bin/sh -c 'echo "x=<$x>"'

name: a lowercase name through a name that holds it, appended to
script:
declare -l x=AbC; declare -n ref=x
ref+=NeW /bin/sh -c 'echo "x=<$x>"'

name: an uppercase name through two names that hold others, appended to
script:
declare -u x=ab; declare -n mid=x; declare -n ref=mid
ref+=cd /bin/sh -c 'echo "x=<$x>"'

name: a readonly name at the end of two names that hold others
script:
readonly dest=old; declare -n mid=dest; declare -n ref=mid
ref=x /bin/echo RAN

name: a readonly name through two names, each assigned
script:
readonly dest=old; declare -n mid=dest; declare -n ref=mid
mid=x ref=y /bin/sh -c 'echo "dest=<$dest>"'
bash:
mid: readonly variable
ref: readonly variable
dest=<>

name: a readonly name that holds an array element
script:
declare -rn ref='a[1]' 2>&1
ref=x /bin/echo RAN

name: a function writing through a name that holds another
a function reading a name that holds another, then changing that one
script:
dest=old; declare -n ref=dest; f() { echo "in=<$ref>"; dest=changed; echo "in2=<$ref>"; }
ref=first f; echo "after=<$dest> ref=<$ref>"

name: a nested function's local, read through a name that holds it
script:
dest=old; declare -n ref=dest; g() { local dest=local; echo "g=<$ref>"; }; f() { echo "f=<$ref>"; g; }
ref=new f

name: a prefix assignment in a function called with one
script:
dest=old; declare -n ref=dest; f() { ref=inner /bin/sh -c 'echo "child dest=<$dest>"'; echo "f dest=<$dest> ref=<$ref>"; }
ref=outer f; echo "after=<$dest>"
bash:
child dest=<inner>
f dest=<outer> ref=<outer>
after=<old>

name: a local name that holds a local one
script:
f() { local dest=old; local -n ref=dest; ref=new /bin/sh -c 'echo "dest=<$dest> ref=<$ref>"'; echo "after=<$dest>"; }
f

name: a name that holds a function's local
script:
declare -n ref=dest; dest=global; f() { local dest=local; ref=new /bin/sh -c 'echo "dest=<$dest>"'; echo "after=<$dest>"; }
f; echo "global=<$dest>"

name: an exported name that holds another
script:
dest=old; declare -nx ref=dest
ref=new /bin/sh -c 'echo "ref=<$ref> dest=<$dest>"'

name: an exported name that holds a second, which holds a third
script:
dest=old; declare -nx ref=mid; declare -n mid=dest
ref=new /usr/bin/env | /bin/grep -E '^(ref|mid|dest)=' | /usr/bin/sort

name: a name that holds an exported one
script:
export dest=old; declare -n ref=dest
ref=new /bin/sh -c 'echo "dest=<$dest>"'; declare -p dest

name: a special builtin with a name that holds another
script:
dest=old; declare -n ref=dest
ref=new :; echo "after=<$dest>"

name: eval with a name that holds another
script:
dest=old; declare -n ref=dest
ref=new eval 'echo "dest=<$dest> ref=<$ref>"'; echo "after=<$dest>"

name: source with a name that holds another
script:
dest=old; declare -n ref=dest; echo 'echo "src dest=<$dest> ref=<$ref>"' >s.sh
ref=new . ./s.sh; echo "after=<$dest>"

name: a redirection's word and a name that holds another
script:
dest=old; declare -n ref=dest
ref=new /bin/echo hi >"$ref"; ls

name: an arithmetic write through a name that holds another
script:
dest=1; declare -n ref=dest
ref=5 b=$((ref+=1)) /bin/sh -c 'echo "dest=<$dest> b=<$b>"'; echo "after=<$dest>"

name: set -x with a name that holds another
script:
dest=old; declare -n ref=dest
set -x
ref=new /bin/true
set +x

name: set -x with an append
script:
x=hello; set -x
x+=world /bin/true
set +x

name: set -x with an integer append
script:
declare -i n=5; set -x
n+=2*3 /bin/true
set +x

name: set -x with an append through a name that holds another
script:
dest=old; declare -n ref=dest; set -x
ref+=new /bin/true
set +x

name: set -x with a compound append
script:
a=zero; set -x
a+=(x y) /bin/true
set +x

name: set -x with two substitutions before a command
script:
set -x
x=$(echo a) y=$(echo b) /bin/true
set +x
bash:
++ echo a
+ x=a
++ echo b
+ y=b
+ /bin/true
+ set +x

name: set -x with two substitutions and no command
script:
set -x
x=$(echo a) y=$(echo b)
set +x
bash:
++ echo a
+ x=a
++ echo b
+ y=b
+ set +x

name: set -x with a readonly name, then a substitution
script:
readonly r=1; set -x
r=2 s=$(echo b) /bin/true
set +x
bash:
r: readonly variable
++ echo b
+ s=b
+ /bin/true
+ set +x

name: set -x with a compound assignment and no command
script:
set -x
a=(x $(echo y))
set +x

name: a compound value appended to an array
script:
declare -a a=(zero one)
a+=(two three) /bin/sh -c 'echo "a=<$a>"'

name: a compound value appended to an associative array
script:
declare -A a=([k]=v [0]=zero)
a+=([k]=new [0]=end) /bin/sh -c 'echo "a=<$a>"'

name: a compound value with quotes and an unset word
script: a=(x "y z" $HOME_NOPE) /bin/sh -c 'echo "a=<$a>"'

name: a compound value is not split, globbed or tilde-expanded
script: touch f1 f2; a=(f*) /bin/sh -c 'echo "a=<$a>"'

name: a compound value's tildes
script: HOME=/h; a=(~ x:~) /bin/sh -c 'echo "a=<$a>"'

name: a compound value's keys
script: k=K v=V; a=([$k]=$v) /bin/sh -c 'echo "a=<$a>"'

name: a compound value's expansions are not split
script: sp='1  2'; a=(x $sp) /bin/sh -c 'echo "a=<$a>"'

name: an empty compound value
script: a=() /bin/sh -c 'echo "a=<$a>"'

name: a compound value appended through a name that holds another
script:
a=zero; declare -n ref=a
ref+=(two three) /bin/sh -c 'echo "a=<$a>"'

name: set -x with a compound value
script:
set -x
a=(x y) /bin/true
set +x

name: a compound value seen by a function
script:
f() { declare -p a; echo "<$a>"; }
a=(x y) f

name: a ring of local names in a function
script:
f() { local -n r1=r2; local -n r2=r1; r1=v /bin/sh -c 'printf "r1=<%s> r2=<%s>\n" "$r1" "$r2"'; }
f; echo S=$?
bash:
warning: r1: circular name reference
r1=<v> r2=<>
S=0

name: a function reading names on a ring
bash:
warning: ref: circular name reference
ref=<new> second=<new> third=<new>

name: a function reading a name that holds one assigned directly
script:
dest=old; declare -n ref=dest; f() { echo "in=<$ref>"; }
dest=new f

name: a nested function reading a name that holds another
script:
dest=old; declare -n ref=dest; g() { echo "g=<$ref> dest=<$dest>"; }; f() { x=1 g; }
ref=outer f

name: an integer append's division by zero before a function
bash:
1/0: division by 0 (error token is "0")
next S=1

name: an integer append's division by zero before a builtin
script:
declare -i x=5
x+=1/0 echo RAN; echo "same S=$?"
echo next S=$?
bash:
1/0: division by 0 (error token is "0")
next S=1

name: an integer append's division by zero after another assignment
script:
declare -i x=5; n=0
( y=$((n+=1)) x+=1/0 /bin/echo RAN >out; echo same ) 2>/dev/null; echo "S=$? n=$n"; ls

name: export lists no prefix assignment
script: x=1 export | /bin/grep -c '^declare -x x=' ; :

name: declare -x lists no prefix assignment
script: x=1 declare -x | /bin/grep -c '^declare -x x=' ; :

name: declare -p names a prefix assignment
script: x=1 declare -p x

name: set lists no prefix assignment
script: x=1 set | /bin/grep -c '^x=' ; :

name: eval's own commands list its prefix assignment
script: x=1 eval 'declare -x' | /bin/grep -c '^declare -x x=' ; :

name: a readonly name's message before a builtin's redirection
script: readonly a=1; a=2 echo hi 2>err; echo S=$?; cat err

name: a readonly name's message before a function's redirection
script: readonly a=1; f() { echo in-f; }; a=2 f 2>err; echo S=$?; cat err

name: an array element's message before a function's redirection
script: f() { echo in-f; }; a[0]=2 f 2>err; echo S=$?; cat err
bash:
`a[0]': not a valid identifier
in-f
S=0

name: a ring's warning before a command's redirection
script: declare -n r1=r2; declare -n r2=r1; r1=v /bin/true 2>err; echo S=$?; cat err
bash:
warning: r1: circular name reference
S=0

name: a ring's warning before its value's substitution
script:
declare -n r1=r2; declare -n r2=r1
r1=$(echo sub >&2; echo v) /bin/sh -c 'echo "r1=<$r1>"' 2>&1
bash:
warning: r1: circular name reference
sub
r1=<v>

name: a readonly name's substitution does not run
script:
readonly a=1; n=0
a=$(echo ran >&2; echo v) /bin/echo cmd

name: a readonly name in posix mode
script:
set -o posix; readonly a=1
a=2 /bin/echo RAN; echo S=$?

name: an integer name assigned through a name, then appended to through it
script:
declare -i x=5; declare -n ref=x
ref=2 ref+=3 /bin/sh -c 'echo "x=<$x>"'
